text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Unions and employers sceptical about government pledge to create some 350,000 jobs for the young in the private sector.
-- Canal Plus sells to Kirch its 37.5 percent in subscriber TV channel Premiere.
-- GAN expected to be in first wave of potential privatisation candidates. French and European authorities seek to reach an agreement on GAN sale before end of month.

-- Germany to adopt 1998 budget project and a mini-budget Friday, German federal deficit expected to reach some 70 billion marks this year. Finance Minister Theo Waigel reaffirms Germany will meet the three percent public deficit target, adds a European currency without France is not being considered.
-- Usinor seen willing to invest up to 3.5 billion francs in privatisation of Spain's steelmaker CSI.
-- Health care spending rose by 2.9 percent in 1996 from 1995, according to national health accounts.
-- Credit Agricole and development bank for small and medium sized companies (BDPME) to launch co-operation in co-financing and guarantees, targetting notably small and medium-sized businesses.
-- Optics group Essilor does not rule out developing through foreign acquisitions notably in the United States, seeks to concentrate on high-value-added products.
-- Compaq chairman Eckhard Pfeiffer in an interview says acquisition of Tandem improves product range, sees French market growth slightly slower than in other countries,
-- Appliance manufacturer Moulinex plant in Argentan to shut down on July 11 as planned.

-- British Airways French airline units Air Liberte and TAT will not break even in 1997 but expect to turn profitable in two years, chairman Marc Rochet said in a radio interview, adding his target was for a three billion francs revenue in two years.
